prompt:
Create a polished fighting-game paired-throw RECEIVER choreography comparison board, landscape 3:2. Two rows A and B, each with THREE full-body paired poses, showing a clear beginning, middle and release with motion arrows. Dark warm-grey uncluttered studio background, thin ground line per row, restrained cream typography. Title "PAIRED THROWS — RECEIVER OPTIONS". Columns "1 / CATCH", "2 / HOLD", "3 / RELEASE". Row labels "A / COLLAR FOLD" and "B / SHOULDER TURN". This is concept review, not a runtime atlas.

Use the two attached references as exact character identities, costume and anime cel-shading style. First is FILLET, female attacker, short black hair, slender arms, cream rolled-sleeve shirt, red leather corset and red shoulder armour on her anatomical LEFT, dark trousers, long dark boots, ragged red/cream cloth. Long knife in anatomical RIGHT hand; shorter knife in LEFT hand. Second is SHARK, male receiver, lean muscular tall build, long swept-back low-volume white hair, BLUE SPORTS GLASSES, sleeveless teal scale vest, bone pauldron, rope belt, grey trousers, brown boots, long hooked staff and small knife. Keep weapons but hold them away from the contact silhouette. Keep both characters the same size in every panel. Fillet to left facing right, Shark to right facing left in every panel. Shark slightly taller; feet full in frame. Adult athletic proportions, crisp black ink, flat shadow shapes.

A / COLLAR FOLD: Catch: Fillet crowds Shark with the outside of her left forearm firmly against his collar/upper chest while keeping her short left knife pointed away; Shark's sternum recoils, hips/knees flex, right staff arm trails low to his outside. Hold: Fillet maintains that same contact landmark; Shark is pulled into a compact forward fold, bent knees, shoulders tense, no floppy limbs. Release: Fillet withdraws to her wide Stalker guard, Shark takes a strong compact chest recoil away from her, shoulders snap back, hips remain grounded, lead knee soft. Clear emotional reaction and weight. This matches an existing damaging capture without an airborne toss.

B / SHOULDER TURN: Catch: same close forearm contact, but Shark's near shoulder is pulled across his torso. Hold: stronger readable ribcage/hip counterrotation and diagonal off-balance compression; feet still on ground, no flipping, no aerial slam, Fillet braces with compact force. Release: Shark twists out into a diagonal chest recoil, one heel skids, staff trails outward. Fillet returns to guard.

Important: these are DIFFERENT RECEIVER silhouettes rather than six neutral standing poses. Add simple curved cream/teal arrows near Shark's shoulder and pelvis in each middle/release panel indicating folding or twisting. Clear snap from hold to recoil, no motion blur, no smears, no ghost duplicate arms, no hit sparks, no blood or injury. Contact hands/forearms must visibly meet bodies with no hovering gap. Keep ALL six pairs fully within separate roomy panels. Three poses per timeline, readable poses at gameplay scale. Preserve correct anatomy and weapon handedness.
notes: Concept board only. Do not install before user selection. Production must restore exact weapon dimensions/handedness and fit the existing capture clocks and root tracks.
